entry.title: fix: read the first card when entering a mode
entry.content:
fix: read the first card when entering a mode

speak() was only wired to go(), grade(), 처음부터 and the V key, so the card
you land on when entering a mode never got read. With 카드마다 자동 읽기 on,
the setting held for every card except the first one you actually look at.

enterMode now speaks after paint(). かな needs no special case -- speak()
already refuses to read a drill glyph before the answer is shown, since that
would hand over the answer.

Verified: entering 단어 requests くろうと.opus and 한자 requests ふむ.opus
immediately, both of which exist on disk, so it is the bundled voice rather
than a fallback; entering かな stays silent; and stepping through three cards
requests exactly one clip each, so nothing plays twice.

entry.title: style: hold the app to its own brief -- two radii, no boxes, one mean…
entry.content:
style: hold the app to its own brief -- two radii, no boxes, one meaning for the accent

The critique scored consistency 2 of 4, and the reason was that the app breaks
rules it wrote down itself. assets/style.css line 4 has said from the start:
"반경: 인터랙티브 요소 3px, 그 외 0. 카드 상자 없음(헤어라인 분리)."

Seven radius values were in use. Three had no basis: a 2px slider track, and
.5rem and .35rem that I added today on the volume popover and the article
number box. All three are var(--r) or 999px now, so the rendered set is 3px,
999px for pills, and 50% for knobs -- the declared set.

Two surfaces were boxes in an app that says it has none. The round summary
built its mistake list as a grid of equal accent-tinted tiles, which is both
the brief's violation and the craft floor's "same-size cards as structure" --
it made a mistake list read as a report card. It is hairline rows now, glyph
and reading left, count right. The meaning mask was a dashed box with a sunken
fill; it is a dashed underline on the page background.

The accent had stopped meaning anything. It exists for one idea -- that a
kanji's Sino-Japanese reading matches the Korean one -- and reading mode was
spending it on a column of six eye toggles plus four dock toggles, all lit at
once. State toggles now read as "brighter" (--fg text, --fg-3 border, no fill)
rather than coloured. Measured: reading mode went from ten accent-wearing
elements to zero, and the word card carries exactly three -- the 한자음 badge,
its value, and the progress bar. Settings buttons keep the accent, where only
one per group is ever on and "this is the current value" is a real meaning.

Verified in both themes across 단어 / 한자 / かな / 읽기: rendered radii are
3px and 999px only, contrast failures 0 and functional text under 11px 0 (the
one flagged item is #btnSpeak's label inside its disabled parent at
opacity .4, which 1.4.3 exempts), and a real drill round renders the mistake
list as hairline rows with border 0, background transparent, radius 0.

entry.title: feat: fix the six critique findings -- autofit floor, opacity contras…
entry.content:
feat: fix the six critique findings -- autofit floor, opacity contrast, tab order, audio state, the inverted ending

Six issues the design critique found. It reports rather than fixes, so these
were open until now.

**Autofit had no lower bound.** app.js:1261 floored --scale at half the base
value, which is a ratio, not a size. At 390x560 the word card put its four
example lines at 8.65px, meta at 6.61px, meaning numerals at 6.15px, and
nothing looked broken. The floor now comes from a measured probe: read the
smallest functional text at the current scale and stop shrinking before it
passes 11px. That lands at 0.724 instead of 0.569 and the example text at
exactly 11px. When even the floor does not fit, the stage scrolls
(`[data-tall="1"]`) rather than shrinking text nobody can read. Six more
`max(11px, …)` floors cover the places --scale multiplies: meta, 한자음, the
meaning numerals, the kanji example rows.

**Ancestor opacity was quietly discounting the contrast tokens.** Fixing
--fg-3 to 4.52:1 does nothing when a parent carries opacity. Measured:
`.art-row.is-next` composited --fg-2 from 7.43:1 down to 2.13:1 at .4 and
1.43:1 at .22, with its border-top at 1.04:1; `.ex-h` fell to 3.83:1 at .82;
`.hjp i.is-kun` to 3.82:1 at .85; the 훈/음 markers sat under .75. Dimming was
the right intent with the wrong instrument -- it scales a value already at the
floor. All four now dim with a colour step instead, and the preview row's
second tier uses size. The only opacity left is :disabled, the loading state,
and a placeholder rule with no placeholder to style.

**The closed settings panel stayed in the tab order.** It closed by transform
alone, so 59 focusable controls sat off-screen and reachable, and a screen
reader announced all of them. It now goes `visibility:hidden` with the
transition delayed past the slide, so the animation still plays. Verified by
calling .focus() on a button inside the closed panel: focus does not move,
activeElement stays BODY. The other two overlays already used display:none.

**Audio had no feedback and swallowed its own failures.** The most frequent
action in the app changed nothing observable, and `a.play()['catch'](function
(){})` meant a blocked autoplay or a muted phone produced no sound, no
message, and no fallback -- a rejected play() never fires onerror, so the
device-TTS path never ran either. Playback now sets `data-speaking` on <html>
from onplaying and clears it on end, which tints the speak button and the
speaker; device TTS feeds the same state through utterance start/end; and a
rejected play() falls back to TTS, or says so when there is no voice either.

**The ending was inverted.** app.js:890 showed the full-screen round summary
only when something had been missed. A perfect round got a 13px toast, so the
only ceremonial screen in the app was the failure report -- 40px type over
boxes counting mistakes. Both endings use the screen now: "한 바퀴 만점" in
the accent with the retry button hidden, or "한 바퀴 완료" as before. While
there, the two denominators got separated -- "5자 중 2자를 틀렸습니다 ·
정답률 71%" counted glyphs on the left and attempts on the right, so the rate
moved to its own line as "입력 n번 중 n번 정답".

**가리기 모드 masked an answer the card prints twice.** Verified: the meaning
masked as "전문가" while the example read "그의 솜씨는 전문가 수준이다." The
example translation and the English gloss hide with it now.

Verified at 390x560 with touch emulation, both themes, across 단어 / 한자 /
かな / 읽기: 0 contrast failures and 0 functional text under 11px, this time
measuring effective contrast with ancestor opacity multiplied in and the
background resolved by walking to the first opaque ancestor -- the earlier
pass compared against html's transparent background, which is why it read
clean. A real drill round to completion produces "한 바퀴 만점 / 5자를 한 번에
다 맞혔습니다 / 입력 5번 중 5번 정답 · 100%" with the retry button hidden. A
sentence clip takes data-speaking 0 -> 1 and back to 0 after its 8.11s.
check-reading.js exits 0; CHECK=1 reports 396 clips and 0 anomalies. The
detector is at its one known false positive.

entry.title: fix: stop the 44px tap overlays stealing each other's taps
entry.content:
fix: stop the 44px tap overlays stealing each other's taps

The touch-target block I added an hour ago gave every dock button and switch a
44x44 ::before hit box. On a single-row dock that is fine, and the comment I
left said so -- "버튼 간격이 6px 이라 겹침도 없다" -- which was sound for the
horizontal gap and blind to the vertical one. At 390px the reading dock wraps
to two rows about 3.8px apart, and each row's buttons claim 8.3px upward, so
the rows ate each other.

The misfiring zone was inside the painted button, not beside it.
elementsFromPoint(130, 686) returned btnRate while sitting 2.1px above
btnAllKo's bottom edge -- 4.5px of 27px, 16.7% of the 번역 button's height,
where a tap changed the playback speed instead of toggling the translation.
Four pairs collided in that mode, and #btnAllKo x #btnFuri collided by 1.5px
regardless of wrapping, because min-width:44px overhangs any label narrower
than 44px.

Checked what actually needed the help, and it was one control:

  reading dock buttons  34-56 x 27   AA pass
  dock icon buttons     42 x 42      AA pass
  settings switches     40 x 22      AA fail by 2px

So the blanket expansion was buying AAA (2.5.5, 44px) for controls that
already cleared AA (2.5.8, 24px), and paying for it with wrong-action taps.
Only .sw keeps a hit box now, grown 3px each way to 28px -- its rows sit 34px
apart, so nothing collides.

Verified at 390x780x2 with touch emulation, which is what makes the rule
apply at all (resizing desktop Chrome to 390px keeps hover:hover and does not
reproduce it): 0 overlapping pairs and 0 controls under the AA floor across
단어, かな, reading in both view modes, and settings open. All four reading
dock buttons receive their own centre tap, (130,686) now resolves to
btnAllKo, and sampling all 143 points inside 번역's painted box sends none of
them to another control.

entry.title: fix: clear the audit findings -- contrast, touch targets, two invisib…
entry.content:
fix: clear the audit findings -- contrast, touch targets, two invisible controls

Ran the Impeccable audit over the app and fixed everything it found. Its
detector went from 28 findings to 1, and that one is a verified false
positive: body{overflow:hidden} is this app's shell (the stage scrolls
internally), and the volume popover opens upward into the stage, staying
inside the viewport -- measured 169px wide and fully painted.

Contrast, one token each way. --fg-3 failed WCAG AA in both themes: 3.30:1 in
dark, 2.73:1 in light, across 36 places. Some of those were reading content,
not chrome -- the example translation, the kana reading and the hangul
pronunciation all sat at 3.55:1, which is a study app losing its own text.
Dark goes #6c6a65 -> #82807b (4.52:1 on --bg-elev), light #8a8f93 -> #666b6f
(4.51:1 on --bg-sunk). Hue held, only lightness moved, and both stay clearly
apart from --fg-2 (6.90-7.63 dark, 5.64-6.74 light) so the three-step
hierarchy survives. Verified: 0 failures across five screens in both themes,
desktop and 390px.

Two controls were invisible. #btnSpeak is a button whose only content is a
.lbl that display:none hides under 400px -- an empty 24x18 box you could tap.
It now carries a waveform SVG and an aria-label, 44x44 on touch. And the
volume popover only had opacity:0 on touch while keeping its layout box, so it
pushed 17px past a 390px viewport on the kana screen and gave the page a
horizontal scrollbar. It is display:none there now. Both regressions were
mine, from earlier today.

Undersized text: the font-picker tile names (9.9px), the kanji example reading
and hangul (10.4px), the 한자음 label (9.9px) and the kbd chips (9.2px) are
functional labels and now floor at 11px. The kana grid labels went 9.6px ->
11.2px and lost the opacity:.6 that was discounting their contrast a second
time; their cells widened to match. Furigana rt stays at 10.2px on purpose --
--rt is tuned so 濁点 and 半濁点 stay apart and the user has a size setting
for it, and the rule is about functional text, not ruby.

Touch targets, 56-71 under 44px per screen -> 0 failures at WCAG 2.5.8 (AA,
24px) everywhere. Height came from real growth where there was room (panel
buttons, the eye toggles, range tracks, the drill input, the wordmark), but
the dock uses an invisible ::before that expands only the tap area: growing
the dock visually pushed the reading footer to two rows, and this keeps it at
one with the same 44px reach. #jumpIn is the single element left under
44 (31x36); widening it grew the counter enough to wrap the footer again, and
36px clears the AA floor by 12px, so it stays.

prefers-reduced-motion no longer kills every transition with .001ms. That
erased the feedback that tells you a switch flipped or a popover opened. Only
the position-moving ones are cut now.

Also, per the skill's craft floor: the ☆/★ favourite glyph is now an SVG pair
matching the other dock icons (unicode glyphs vary in width and stroke between
fonts, and every neighbour was already drawn), the popover dropped its 28px
shadow to keep the hairline -- this app's own stated world is "no card boxes,
hairline separation" and pairing both is a generated-UI tell -- and the
browser surfaces nobody draws now follow the palette: ::selection, the
scrollbar, link colour and underline offset.

entry.title: fix: attach the volume popover to the speaker button
entry.content:
fix: attach the volume popover to the speaker button

It floated as a detached box with a dead 7px gap, and that gap was also a
bug: crossing it left both the button and the popover unhovered, so the
popover closed before the pointer arrived.

- A caret now points down at the button, drawn as a border-colour triangle
  with a background-colour one overlapping it by 1px so the bubble keeps its
  outline.
- A 9px strip covers the 7px gap while hovering, so the pointer never leaves
  the hover target on the way up. It only exists during hover, so it does not
  swallow clicks above the dock the rest of the time.
- The popover scales from the button (transform-origin bottom center) instead
  of sliding in from nowhere, and the button keeps its hover border while the
  pointer is in the popover, so the two read as one control.

The caret first came out white and upside down: `border-width:7px` in the
later rule overrode `border-bottom-width:0` from the shared one, so the bottom
border rendered in currentColor. Both widths are now written in one
declaration.

Verified with the button hovered: popover opacity 1 / pointer-events auto,
gap 7px against a 9px bridge, caret borders 7px 7px 0 in --line over 6px 6px 0
in --bg-elev, button border on --line.

entry.title: feat: volume slider on the speaker button, 0 mutes
entry.content:
feat: volume slider on the speaker button, 0 mutes

Hovering the speaker in the dock now slides out a popover above it with the
volume slider and the percentage. Click keeps toggling mute, so nothing about
the old behaviour changed.

Dragging to 0 mutes and raising from 0 unmutes, which needed one rule: S.vol
never stores 0. Mute lives in S.tts as before, so the slider shows 0 while
S.vol keeps the level to come back to -- mute then unmute returns to 45%, not
to some default.

Both sliders (dock and settings) go through setVol and redraw each other, so
they cannot drift. The settings one no longer uses rng(), which wrote S.vol
directly and knew nothing about muting.

Touch gets no popover: with no hover, a tap would have to both open the
popover and mute, and those want the same gesture. Phones have a hardware
volume and the settings panel still has the slider -- YouTube makes the same
call. Verified under touch emulation: hover:hover false, popover opacity 0 and
pointer-events none, and the button still toggles mute; the 42x42 target and
the footer layout are unchanged at 390px.

Also dropped two more guards that assumed device TTS was the only sound
source: the mute button was disabled and toggleMute() returned early when the
machine had no Japanese voice, which left bundled clips playing with no way to
stop them.

Persistence checked past the 250ms save debounce: 45% -> {vol:0.45,tts:true},
0 -> {vol:0.45,tts:false}, unmute -> {vol:0.45,tts:true}.

entry.title: fix: bundled word audio was switched off by two unrelated settings
entry.content:
fix: bundled word audio was switched off by two unrelated settings

speak() only reached playClip when it had exactly one thing to say:

    if (q.length === 1) { playClip(wordClip(t), t); return; }
    speakChain(q, speakSeq);

So turning on 단어 두 번 읽기 or 예문도 읽기 pushed a second item and the
whole card fell to device TTS. Kanji mode lost it the same way via 예문도
읽기. Either switch silently took bundled audio to 0%, which is why 60 cards
in a row could play no Gemini voice.

sayChain replaces that. Items carry {t, clip}; each one plays from a clip when
the file exists and falls back to device TTS on its own error, so a chain can
mix the two. Example sentences pass clip:0 -- no clips were made for them --
so they go straight to the device voice with no wasted lookup.

Also relaxed the guard at the top of speak(): it required voices.length, so a
machine with no Japanese system voice played nothing even though the bundled
clips were sitting right there. Only S.tts gates it now; a missing device
voice is handled per item.

Verified in Chrome across both modes and all four switch combinations -- every
one attempts a clip now. One card with both switches on:
  음원 じょじょに / 음원 じょじょに / 음원 じょこう→기기 / 음원 そろそろ→기기
and in word mode 住: 음원 じゅう twice, then the example sentence straight to
the device voice.

Coverage, measured, for the record: kanji mode 2094/2142 = 98%. Word deck
2820/9543 = 30%, capped at 51% once all 3718 kanji-example readings exist --
the deck is 9543 words and only kanji examples were generated.

entry.title: fix: match r39239 sentence 2 to what the voice actually says
entry.content:
fix: match r39239 sentence 2 to what the voice actually says

The voice ends that sentence 「とされています」 while the screen read
「とされている」. The data was not at fault -- s[1].k held the plain form, so
the model paraphrased it into polite speech on its own. A learner reading one
form and hearing another learns the wrong thing.

Three parts:

The sentence text and its kana now carry 「とされています」. CC BY permits this
(it is not NoDerivatives) but §3(a)(1)(B) wants the modification indicated, so
ATTRIBUTION §6 now says the body text gets adjusted to the audio, lists this
edit, and warns that data/reading.js is generated -- rebuilding the deck drops
hand edits and they have to be fed back from that list.

The article prompt now adds 「書かれている語尾をそのまま読み、です・ます調に
言い換えないでください」. 「ニュースを読むように」 stays: dropping it changes
the delivery and new clips would not sit next to the 395 already made.

DATA_V and AUDIO_V are now separate. One shared value meant editing a single
sentence re-downloaded all 16MB of audio; AUDIO_V stays at v=30 so existing
caches survive, and only bumps when a clip is overwritten.

Verified: check-reading.js exits 0 (46 articles, 350 sentences), CHECK=1
reports 396 clips and 0 anomalies, and the card renders 「…とされています。」
while still requesting r39239-2.opus?v=30.

Not verified: that the clip says what the report says. There is no offline
transcription here, so the other 395 clips cannot be swept for the same
defect -- clip duration does not separate it from ordinary pausing (this
sentence ranks 41st by excess length, behind clips that are simply slower).

entry.title: feat: speed control in the reading footer, 0.5x to 1.5x
entry.content:
feat: speed control in the reading footer, 0.5x to 1.5x

The speed already existed as a slider buried in settings, and playClip was
already applying it. What was missing was reaching it while reading.

One button that cycles 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 / 1.25 / 1.5, plus [ and ] for a single
step. Five buttons do not fit the footer. It drives the same S.rate as the
settings slider rather than a reading-only copy, so the two cannot disagree --
the slider and its label are written back on each change. Changing speed while
a sentence is playing retunes the live clip instead of waiting for the next one.

[ and ] survive Hangul input: 두벌식 puts no jamo on those keys, unlike the
letter shortcuts that need the e.code fallback.

Verified in Chrome:
- button cycles 1 -> 1.25 -> 1.5 -> 0.5 -> 0.75 -> 1, [ and ] clamp at the ends
- settings slider follows: rRate 150, vRate "1.50배"
- at 0.5x a clip reports playbackRate 0.5 with preservesPitch true, so pitch
  accent is not dropped an octave
- pressing ] mid-sentence moves the playing clip from 0.5 to 1

Footer at 390px needed the readacts gap and button padding tightened to keep
one row with a fourth button (195px in the common case). The one case that
still wraps -- one-sentence mode showing "문장 12/13" -- wraps identically
with the button hidden, so it predates this.

entry.title: fix: the quota is a rolling 24h window -- keep the driver running
entry.content:
fix: the quota is a rolling 24h window -- keep the driver running

I had this wrong twice. The docs say RPD "resets at midnight Pacific", and
the burst at 09-16 16:00 looked like confirmation. It wasn't a reset: it was
the 95 requests spent at 09-15 16:00 ageing out.

Clip timestamps per hour, converted to requests:

  09-15 17시 1  ->  09-16 17시 2
  09-15 18시 5  ->  09-16 18시 4
  09-15 19시 0  ->  09-16 19시 0
  09-15 20시 2  ->  09-16 20시 1
  09-15 21시 0  ->  09-16 21시 0

Hours that spent nothing yesterday hand back nothing today. So the driver
should stay up rather than being started at a guessed reset time -- it has to
be running at the minute a slot frees. 140 clips appeared between 17:32 and
20:40 today while mine was stopped, which is the cost of guessing.

Also added an instance lock. Two sessions share this checkout, and two
drivers would compute the same todo list and generate the same chunks twice.
mkdir is the atomic primitive; a stale lock whose pid is gone gets cleared.
Verified: second instance prints "이미 돌고 있다 (pid 8026)" and exits 1.

Includes the 140 word clips (800 -> 940).

entry.title: fix: pick word boundaries by gap length, not by every silence
entry.content:
fix: pick word boundaries by gap length, not by every silence

Half of today's requests were thrown away. The slicer cut at every detected
silence, but a geminate consonant is real silence inside a word -- がっこう
holds a ~0.15s stop -- so 20 words came back as 21 or 22 segments and the
chunk was discarded. The log from one round: 19 of 39 chunks lost, 15 of them
reporting "구간 21개인데 단어는 20개".

sliceWords now finds every silence, drops the leading and trailing ones, and
uses only the n-1 longest as boundaries. Short internal stops lose to the
~3s gaps the prompt asks for. A segment under 0.15s means the boundaries were
chosen wrong, so the chunk is still discarded -- misaligned word audio is
exactly what a learner cannot detect.

Checked against the 37 chunk wavs this round left in TMPDIR:
- chunks yielding a usable 20-way split: 17 -> 35
- on the 17 the old method also handled, 19 of 20 segments match to the
  millisecond; the 20th differs by 0.136s because the new code trims 0.14s
  of leading silence the old one kept
